a.name: Shop door bell
a.desc: The little bell above a shop door jingles as someone steps in.
a.note: Main: ryuuzan shop door bell (two strikes, 0 dB at 30 and 210 ms). Split into two layers so the second strike sits 4 dB lower and the loudest point stays at the start; the second layer starts on a zero crossing at 204.1 ms and is placed in its natural time (no click at the join). Pitched -2 st to warm it. A quiet wooden door latch (SpliceSound) underneath for the door.

layers.credit: "Julian's Door - open and close with latch.wav" by SpliceSound, CC0, https://freesound.org/people/SpliceSound/sounds/218323

b.name: Door swings open
b.desc: A wooden door latch clacks and the door swings open with a soft creak.
b.note: Main: Kenney RPG doorOpen_1. Layer 1 is its first latch clack (137.7-192.1 ms); layer 2 is the rest (second clack and the creak) 7 dB lower, so the opening clack is the loudest point (rise was 66 ms with one layer). Both cuts are on quiet zero crossings.

c.name: Quick friendly raps
c.desc: Three quick, light knocks, like a friend at the door.
c.note: Main: craigsmith 'R09-26-Various Knocks' (one knuckle knock with a short wooden resonance, crest 11.5 dB, so it reaches the loudness target; the drier wjtaylor knocks could not). Used twice 160 ms apart, pitched +2/+3 and high-passed at 250 Hz for a light, bright knock; the second is 2 dB lower so the first stays loudest.

a.name: Low bell toll
a.desc: One old bell rung low, slowly fading away.
a.note: Main: lazymonk 'Door Bell old style' (struck mechanical bell, 2 ms rise, natural decay), pitched -5 st so it reads as the lower, sadder answer to the join bell. Cut at 750 ms with a long fade.

layers.credit: "Door Bell old style.wav" by lazymonk, CC0, https://freesound.org/people/lazymonk/sounds/214306

b.name: Door shuts
b.desc: A wooden door swings shut and its latch clicks closed.
b.note: Main: Kenney RPG doorClose_1 from 170 ms (the slam and latch, 0 dB at 190-260 ms). A low thud from NicholasJudy567 'Wooden Door Closes 2' under it for weight.

c.name: Soft gust away
c.desc: A soft, low gust of air, like someone slipping out.

a.name: Clear bell ring
a.desc: A small brass bell struck once, clear and sure.
a.note: Main: AlaskaRobotics service bell ring (2 ms rise, steady ring with gentle beating), pitched -3 st and low-passed so it sounds older and less like a hotel desk; cut at 800 ms with a long fade.

b.name: Heavy latch locks
b.desc: A heavy gate latch drops shut with a solid wooden thunk.
b.note: Main: mhtaylor67 'Gate Latch' (sharp, 11 ms peak). TylerAM 'Thump; close' and Kenney Impact wood heavy (pitched -2) under it for a solid wooden body.

c.name: Key turns, bell tings
c.desc: A key clicks in an old lock, then a tiny bell rings.
c.note: Main: Astounded 'Door_Lock_unlock' (two key clicks, 0 and 50 ms). A small bright bell ting (sqeeeek) follows at 110 ms, a little lower so the click stays the loudest point.

a.name: Dull falling bell
a.desc: Two muffled bell clunks, the second lower, like something going wrong.
a.note: Main: Kenney Impact bell heavy 002, pitched -4 and low-passed to kill the ring; then bell heavy 003 at 170 ms, pitched -8 and 3 dB lower, so it falls. Dead and dull, not a buzzer.

b.name: Stuck latch
b.desc: A latch clicks, then a dull knock: the door will not open.
b.note: metal latch then a dull wood knock

c.name: Dull double knock
c.desc: Two slow, heavy, muffled knocks on a thick door.
c.note: Main: kbnevel 'DoorKnock_heavy', first two knocks as separate layers (the second cut on a silent zero crossing at 222.6 ms, placed at its natural 244 ms, 4 dB lower so the first stays loudest), pitched -2. A low-passed heavy thud (thud2) under the first knock for a dead, heavy body (and to reach loudness).
